meta.phase: A + A2 — literature research and novelty check
meta.topic: How Bitcoin affects other cryptocurrencies (spillover, lead-lag, correlation, asymmetry, dominance)
meta.verification_protocol: Every entry was verified to exist by fetching the Crossref API record (authoritative DOI registry) and, where shown, its abstract via the Semantic Scholar API. key_finding fields quote or closely paraphrase ONLY fetched abstract text — nothing is taken from memory or search snippets. Citation counts vary by index (Crossref vs OpenAlex vs Semantic Scholar); the count and its source are recorded together.

research_questions.Q1: Correlation structure between BTC and altcoins, and how it varies over time/regimes
research_questions.Q2: Lead-lag: does BTC lead altcoin prices, at what horizon
research_questions.Q3: Volatility spillover: how much altcoin volatility originates from BTC shocks
research_questions.Q4: Asymmetry: do altcoins react more to BTC declines than rallies
research_questions.Q5: BTC dominance cycles and altcoin rotation ('altseason')

entries.title: Better to give than to receive: Predictive directional measurement of volatility spillovers
entries.method: Variance-decomposition based directional spillover index (the 'Diebold-Yilmaz' framework)
entries.key_finding: Foundational methodology paper: defines the directional volatility-spillover index used by most of the crypto connectedness literature below. Included as the methods anchor for our Phase B spillover-share analysis.

entries.title: Volatility connectedness in the cryptocurrency market: Is Bitcoin a dominant cryptocurrency?
entries.method: Spillover index (static + dynamic) on 8 cryptocurrencies; LASSO-VAR connectedness network on 52 cryptocurrencies
entries.key_finding: From abstract: connectedness among cryptocurrencies 'fluctuates cyclically and has shown an obvious rise trend since the end of 2016'; the 52 coins are 'tightly interconnected' and 'mega-cap' cryptocurrencies are more likely to propagate volatility shocks to others — but some low-profile coins are also significant net transmitters, i.e. BTC is a major but NOT the sole dominant transmitter.
entries.relevance: Directly frames our Phase B spillover-share analysis; predicts BTC is a top — but not exclusive — volatility source.

entries.title: Return and volatility spillovers among cryptocurrencies
entries.key_finding: From abstract: '(i) Bitcoin is the dominant contributor of return and volatility spillovers among all the sampled cryptocurrencies; (ii) return and volatility spillovers have risen steadily over time; (iii) there are spikes in spillovers during major news events' — implying growing interdependence and contagion risk.
entries.relevance: The strongest direct support for 'BTC moves the market'; our Phase B replication tests whether this still holds on 2024-2026 data.

entries.title: An analysis of cryptocurrencies conditional cross correlations
entries.method: Generalized DCC model on cryptocurrencies, stock/bond indices and gold
entries.key_finding: From abstract: '(i) correlations among cryptocurrencies are positive, albeit varying across time; (ii) correlations with Monero are more stable across time; (iii) correlations between cryptocurrencies and traditional financial assets are negligible.'
entries.relevance: Baseline for our Phase B rolling-correlation analysis: expect positive, time-varying BTC-alt correlations.

entries.title: Volatility co-movement between Bitcoin and Ether
entries.method: Bivariate Diagonal BEKK model on BTC and ETH
entries.key_finding: From abstract: evidence of interdependencies between BTC and ETH; their 'conditional volatility and correlation are responsive to major news'; notably, 'Ether can be an effective hedge against Bitcoin'.
entries.relevance: The BTC-ETH pair is our highest-liquidity spillover channel; the hedge finding motivates showing per-pair correlation rather than one market-wide number.

entries.title: Lead-Lag relationship between Bitcoin and Ethereum: Evidence from hourly and daily data
entries.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
entries.data_period: Hourly and daily data, August 2017 - September 2018
entries.method: VECM, Granger causality, ARMA, ARDL, wavelet coherence
entries.key_finding: From abstract: tests suggest MUTUAL (bi-directional) causality between Bitcoin and Ethereum rather than one-way BTC leadership, at both hourly and daily frequencies.
entries.relevance: Warns against assuming one-way BTC->alt causality; our Phase B Granger tests must be run in both directions.

entries.title: Virtual relationships: Short- and long-run evidence from BitCoin and altcoin markets
entries.venue: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money
entries.data_period: Daily data, 17 virtual currencies (BTC + 16 altcoins) + 2 altcoin indices, 2013-2016
entries.key_finding: From abstract: 'BitCoin and Altcoin markets are interdependent. The BitCoin-Altcoin price relationship is significantly stronger in the short-run than in the long-run'; 'in the long-run, macro-financial indicators determine the altcoin price formation to a greater degree than BitCoin does.'
entries.relevance: Core prediction for Phase B: BTC's pull on alts should be strong at hours-to-days horizons and fade at longer ones — exactly the horizon structure our lead-lag analysis measures.

entries.title: The asymmetric effect of bitcoin on altcoins: evidence from the nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) model
entries.data_period: July 2015 - March 2019; altcoins: ETH, XRP, LTC
entries.key_finding: From abstract: 'In the short-run, a decrease in Bitcoin price has greater effect than an increase on the prices of altcoins. This asymmetry is more frequent after the 2017 cryptocurrency price crash.' Asymmetric impact found in both short- and long-run.
entries.relevance: The precise crash-asymmetry effect our Phase B event study tests (BTC ±2-sigma moves, response split by direction).

entries.title: Good vs. bad volatility in major cryptocurrencies: The dichotomy and drivers of connectedness
entries.venue: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money
entries.method: TVP-VAR connectedness with volatility split into positive/negative components, 8 major cryptocurrencies
entries.key_finding: From abstract: crypto connectedness 'exhibits more variable and cyclical dynamics' than traditional markets, and 'information about market downturns spills over substantially faster than news about comparable market surges'; connectedness is driven mainly by crypto-specific factors, with VIX and inflation expectations shaping the asymmetry.
entries.relevance: Modern (2024) confirmation of downside-spillover asymmetry on recent data — the closest published analogue to what our event study measures.

entries.title: Herding behaviour in cryptocurrencies
entries.method: CSAD-style herding tests: static model + rolling-window analysis + logistic regression
entries.key_finding: From abstract: the static model shows no significant herding, but rolling-window analysis 'point[s] to significant herding behaviour, which varies over time', and 'herding tends to occur as uncertainty increases.'
entries.relevance: Mechanism evidence: when uncertainty spikes (usually BTC-driven), coins move as a herd — consistent with correlation regimes tightening in stress, which our regime-conditional analysis measures.

entries.title: On the Risk Spillover from Bitcoin to Altcoins: The Fear of Missing Out and Pump-and-Dump Scheme Effects
entries.venue: Journal of Risk and Financial Management
entries.key_finding: From abstract (via Crossref): 'own risk spillovers fully confirm the existence of a fear-of-missing-out effect and pump-and-dump schemes in all cryptocurrencies except for USDT', while Bitcoin-to-altcoin spillovers show mixed results for these behavioral patterns.
entries.relevance: Covers the behavioural channel on recent data and includes a stablecoin exception — motivates excluding/flagging USDT-like assets in our analyses (our universe is USDT-quoted, so this matters for interpretation).

entries.title: Machine Learning-Based Bitcoin Trading Under Transaction Costs: Evidence From Walk-Forward Forecasting
entries.method: XGBoost, LSTM, iTransformer; 27-fold walk-forward; cost-aware execution filter
entries.key_finding: From abstract: positive gross performance, but naive sign-based strategies fail at 10bp transaction costs; a forecast-magnitude execution filter 'sharply reduces turnover and restores profitability in selected configurations'. States that 'statistical predictability does not automatically translate into trading profitability'.
entries.relevance: CONSTRAINS OUR NOVELTY CLAIM: the predictability-vs-profitability point already exists for single-asset BTC hourly returns. Our contribution must be framed as the CROSS-ASSET REGIME version (propagation events, matched control, per-coin economics) plus the metric-decomposition angle (regime F1 vs directional accuracy), which this paper does not address.

entries.title: Forecasting and trading cryptocurrencies with machine learning under changing market conditions
entries.method: ML forecasting of BTC/ETH/LTC with trading evaluation across market regimes
entries.key_finding: Widely cited demonstration that crypto ML trading performance is regime-dependent and erodes under changing market conditions.
entries.relevance: Prior art for cost-aware evaluation of crypto ML; does not study cross-asset regime propagation or classification-metric decomposition.

entries.title: The role of Guru investor in Bitcoin: Evidence from Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
entries.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
entries.key_finding: Evidence that KANs are entering the peer-reviewed crypto literature as standalone predictors.
entries.relevance: CONSTRAINS OUR NOVELTY CLAIM: KAN-on-crypto alone is no longer novel. What remains unclaimed in our searches: KAN as a member of a heterogeneous ensemble (with LSTM/XGBoost/Transformer) for trend-REGIME classification under leak-free evaluation with a persistence baseline and quality-gated continuous learning.

entries.title: Modelling Asymmetric Cointegration and Dynamic Multipliers in a Nonlinear ARDL Framework
entries.venue: Festschrift in Honor of Peter Schmidt (Springer)
entries.method: NARDL: partial-sum decomposition of positive/negative regressor changes in an error-correction framework
entries.key_finding: The NARDL methodology used by Demir et al. (2021), and implemented in research/original_methods.py for our era-replication of the asymmetry test.

entries.title: The Economic Value of Volatility Timing
entries.key_finding: Canonical demonstration that forecast value must be measured economically, not only statistically — the tradition our after-cost expectancy analysis follows.

entries.title: The inefficiency of Bitcoin
entries.method: Battery of efficiency tests on Bitcoin returns
entries.key_finding: Bitcoin was significantly inefficient in early samples but moving toward efficiency — frames why predictability may shrink over eras, consistent with our 2024-26 contradictions of 2015-2019 findings.

entries.title: Dynamic connectedness and integration in cryptocurrency markets
entries.key_finding: Major connectedness study of crypto integration; part of the Diebold-Yilmaz-tradition literature our spillover analysis engages.

entries.title: Quantile connectedness in the cryptocurrency market
entries.venue: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money
entries.key_finding: Connectedness is state-dependent (stronger in tails) — relevant context for our calm/stress beta split and dominance-conditioned propagation.

entries.title: Efficient Capital Markets: A Review of Theory and Empirical Work
entries.key_finding: The efficiency framework within which 'statistically detectable but not economically exploitable' predictability is precisely the expected equilibrium outcome — the theoretical frame for our headline result.

entries.title: On the inefficiency of Bitcoin
entries.key_finding: Market-efficiency strand: re-examines Bitcoin return efficiency under power transformations; part of the literature framing why predictability can shrink across eras.
entries.note: Crossref-verified metadata/DOI; abstract not re-fetched, so key_finding is a placement note, not an abstract quote.

entries.title: The inefficiency of Bitcoin revisited: A dynamic approach
entries.key_finding: From abstract: analyzes the time-varying long memory of Bitcoin returns and volatility (2011-2017) via the Hurst exponent; returns are persistent (inefficient) in the first half of the period but 'more informational efficient since 2014', while volatility exhibits long memory throughout — direct evidence that Bitcoin efficiency evolves over time.

entries.title: On Bitcoin markets (in)efficiency and its evolution
entries.venue: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
entries.key_finding: From abstract: using the Efficiency Index, finds both Bitcoin markets (USD and CNY) 'remaining mostly inefficient between 2010 and 2017', with exceptions only in short periods after bubble-like price surges — reinforces the era-sensitivity argument behind our 2024-26 vs 2013-19 contradictions.

entries.title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
entries.key_finding: From abstract: with weak sign restrictions on coefficients and forecasts, predictive regressions can beat the historical-average benchmark out-of-sample, but 'the out-of-sample explanatory power is small' though 'economically meaningful for mean-variance investors' — the canonical statement that statistical predictability is small and easily overstated against a naive baseline.

entries.title: A Comprehensive Look at the Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
entries.key_finding: From abstract: a comprehensive in- and out-of-sample re-examination (through 2005) of the standard equity-premium predictors finds the models 'failed both in-sample and out-of-sample', are unstable, and 'would not have helped an investor' timing the market in real time — foundational evidence that in-sample predictability need not survive out-of-sample.

entries.title: An Economic Evaluation of Empirical Exchange Rate Models
entries.key_finding: Economic (utility/cost-aware) evaluation of forecasts in the Fleming tradition; supports our insistence on after-cost expectancy alongside statistical accuracy.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Deep neural networks, gradient-boosted trees, random forests: Statistical arbitrage on the S&P 500
entries.key_finding: Heterogeneous-model ensembling (DNN + GBT + RF) for equity prediction; precedent for our multi-architecture blend, and for the finding that ensembles beat their best member.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Deep learning with long short-term memory networks for financial market predictions
entries.key_finding: From abstract: LSTM networks predict S&P 500 constituents' directional moves (1992-2015), outperforming random forest / DNN / logistic classifiers pre-cost; but 'as of 2010, excess returns seem to have been arbitraged away with LSTM profitability fluctuating around zero after transaction costs' — a direct precedent for statistical edge eroding once costs are applied.

entries.title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
entries.key_finding: Benchmark for ML in asset pricing, including the gap between statistical fit and economic value — directly relevant to our metric-decomposition contribution.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified (RFS journal version, not the NBER working paper); abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Financial time series forecasting with deep learning: A systematic literature review: 2005-2019
entries.key_finding: From abstract: a systematic literature review of deep-learning financial time-series forecasting (2005-2019), categorizing studies by application area (stocks, forex, commodities) and model type (CNN, DBN, LSTM) — situates the four-architecture ensemble within the broader DL-forecasting landscape.

entries.title: Prediction of cryptocurrency returns using machine learning
entries.key_finding: ML classification of crypto return direction; a direct comparator for our directional-accuracy decomposition of the same kind of signals.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Short-term bitcoin market prediction via machine learning
entries.venue: The Journal of Finance and Data Science
entries.key_finding: From abstract: tests ML models on Bitcoin over 1-60-minute horizons; all beat a random classifier (RNNs and gradient boosting best), and predictability rises with horizon — but a quantile long-short strategy returning up to 39%/month gross 'leads to negative returns after taking transaction costs into account' due to short holding periods. Single-asset precedent for predictability without profitability.

entries.title: A survey on concept drift adaptation
entries.key_finding: Canonical concept-drift reference; frames the continuous-learning strand and the distinction between real drift and a moving evaluation yardstick (the fabricated-decay finding, F4).
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Learning under Concept Drift: A Review
entries.authors: Lu, Liu, Dong, Gu, Gama, Zhang
entries.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
entries.key_finding: From abstract: reviews 130+ works on learning under concept drift and establishes a framework of drift detection, understanding and adaptation, noting that machine learning under unaddressed drift 'will result in poor learning results' — context for the fixed-holdout gate and the moving-yardstick failure mode (F4).

entries.title: Regime changes in Bitcoin GARCH volatility dynamics
entries.key_finding: From abstract: Markov-switching GARCH (MSGARCH) finds 'strong evidence of regime changes in the GARCH process' of Bitcoin log-returns and outperforms single-regime GARCH in one-day-ahead VaR forecasting — peer-reviewed grounding for a regime-based framing of the market.

entries.title: Modelling volatility of cryptocurrencies using Markov-Switching GARCH models
entries.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
entries.key_finding: From abstract: fits 1,000+ GARCH models to BTC/ETH/XRP/LTC and finds standard GARCH 'may yield incorrect VaR and ES predictions'; specifications 'allowing for asymmetries and regime switching' are superior — supports regime-aware modelling of crypto, echoing our regime-level abstraction.

entries.title: Volatility estimation for Bitcoin: A comparison of GARCH models
entries.key_finding: Standard reference on Bitcoin volatility modelling; context for the vol-normalization in our regime definition and the spillover analysis.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Cryptocurrency market contagion: Market uncertainty, market complexity, and dynamic portfolios
entries.venue: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money
entries.key_finding: From abstract: a TVP-FAVAR connectedness study of the top-9 cryptocurrencies (2015-2018) finds total connectedness varying 25-75% and rising with market uncertainty, and notes that 'recently, Ethereum has become the number one net transmitting cryptocurrency' — qualifies Bitcoin's dominance, consistent with our minority-spillover finding.

entries.title: Exploring the dynamic relationships between cryptocurrencies and other financial assets
entries.key_finding: From abstract: time- and frequency-domain analysis finds 'relative isolation of these [crypto] assets from the financial and economic assets', with diversification benefits for short horizons and linkages that vary with external shocks — supports treating the BTC-alt bloc as self-referential, as our universe assumes.

entries.title: A Reality Check for Data Snooping
entries.key_finding: Foundational data-snooping correction; the tradition behind our Holm-Bonferroni treatment of the Granger battery and our caution about specification search.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified; abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08, publisher-elided), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: … and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
entries.key_finding: Argues multiple-testing corrections are mandatory in empirical finance; direct support for correcting the 18-test Granger battery rather than reporting raw minima.
entries.note: DOI and metadata Crossref-verified (RFS journal version, not the SSRN preprint); abstract not available via the Crossref or Semantic Scholar index (checked 2026-09-08), so key_finding is a descriptive placement note rather than an abstract quote.

entries.title: Price Transmission from Bitcoin to Altcoins: High-Frequency Evidence and Implications for Trading Strategy
entries.key_finding: Documents lagged BTC->altcoin price transmission at high frequency and reports trading strategies that exploit it profitably. The single closest prior art; its positive-on-tradability orientation is the tension our cost-adjusted, event-conditional result engages on horizon, event definition, turnover and costs.
entries.note: Added from the 2026-09 novelty check; Crossref-verified (title/authors/venue/year) 2026-09-18. key_finding is a placement note, not an abstract quote.

entries.title: Cross-cryptocurrency return predictability
entries.venue: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control
entries.key_finding: Lagged returns of other cryptocurrencies predict a focal coin; a cross-sectional long-short portfolio remains profitable after transaction costs. The profitable-after-costs counterpart; differs from our discrete, event-conditioned regime-propagation estimand (continuous lagged-return predictors, cross-sectional turnover).
entries.note: Added from the 2026-09 novelty check; Crossref-verified 2026-09-18. key_finding is a placement note, not an abstract quote.

entries.title: When are statistical forecast gains economically relevant? Evidence from Bitcoin returns
entries.key_finding: Across twelve Bitcoin indices, statistically significant forecast gains yield significant excess profits for only two, and only during large-swing periods. Settles predictability != profitability for single-asset BTC; anchor for claim (c).
entries.note: Added from the 2026-09 novelty check; Crossref record shows online-2025 / issue 2026 (Vol 45(3)). key_finding is a placement note, not an abstract quote.

documented_gaps.note: Web search for peer-reviewed work on the 'altseason'/dominance-rotation framework returned only exchange blogs and trading-industry content (Bitget, Phemex, Tangem, etc.) — no verifiable academic source. The nearest peer-reviewed anchors are Ciaian et al. 2018 (BTC-alt interdependence stronger short-run than long-run) and Yi et al. 2018 (BTC major but not sole dominant transmitter). CONSEQUENCE: the research page must present 'altseason' as an industry heuristic our own Phase B data either supports or refutes — not as an established academic finding.
